item.title: Indivisible Yolo’s No Kings Vote Early Events — Sat Oct 17 — G Street Plaza
item.description: Indivisible Yolo will host three No Kings Vote Early events across Davis, West Sacramento and Woodland on Oct. 17. The mass participation events will build upon the energy of previous mass protests as the group works to turn protest power into early voter action. Local residents are invited to attend one or more of the three community events and bring their ballots to submit. Hosted information booths will provide voter assistance, including voter registration, details on when and where to vote, as well as information on California ballot initiatives and efforts to combat voter suppression. The Woodland No Kings Vote Early event will take place from 10am-1pm at the Old Courthouse, 725 Court Street. The West Sacramento event will take place from 10am-2pm at Trinity Presbyterian Church, 1500 Park Boulevard. The Davis event will take place from 2-4pm at G Street Plaza, 301 G Street. To sign up for one or more events, visit https://www.indivisibleyolo.org/no-kings-vote-early. Indivisible

item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Sat Oct 17, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Sat Oct 17, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Birds & Bikes — Sat Oct 17, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop

item.title: Making Sense of Scientific Articles: A Survival Kit for Reading Research Papers — Wed Oct 28, 2:30 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
Struggling to make sense of scientific papers? You're not alone! Scientific articles can be intimidating, but knowing how to approach them makes a big difference.
Join students from the College of Biological Sciences' BioInnovation Group for a workshop designed to help you tackle scientific papers with confidence. Learn how to find research articles that interest you, navigate the different sections of a scientific paper, and break down complex research into your own words. We'll share practical tips and tricks to make reading scientific literature feel a little less overwhelming.
Whether you're reading papers for a class, exploring a research topic, or just curious about scientific discoveries, this workshop will help you build skills you can use throughout your academic journey.

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

item.title: Free Yoga Practice — Thu Oct 29, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community 🌀 **Move with intention. Connect with your body. Celebrate community.**
Join us every **Thursday at 6 PM** for an embodied yoga practice designed to help you release tension, ground yourself, and cultivate presence. This is a trauma-informed, all-levels class, no prior yoga experience needed. Expect a Hatha-Vinyasa flow, breathwork, and a space to listen to your body’s wisdom.
🌿 **Every last Thursday of the month, stay after class for a community potluck dinner!**
📍 **Location**: 727 T St. Sacramento CA 95811 ✨ **All our events are free. Donations are welcome.** 📩 **Questions? Reach out at** embody.iama@gmail.com 🔗 **Follow us on Instagram:** [@embody.iama](https://www.instagram.com/embody.iama)
Source: Meetup: Mindful Embodied Spirituality

item.title: Davis Farmers Market – Wednesday Evenings (50th Anniversary Year) — Wed Dec 23, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
The Davis Farmers Market continues every Wednesday in Central Park with new fall hours! Beginning Wednesday, September 2, the Wednesday market will be open from 3:00–6:00 PM, replacing the extended 4:00–8:00 PM Picnic in the Park hours. Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. It’s a great opportunity to stock up for the week, meet up with friends, support local growers and food makers, and enjoy a beautiful afternoon in Central Park. The Davis Farmers Market is celebrating its 50th Anniversary in 2026, marking five decades of bringing fresh food, local farmers and the Davis community together. Wednesday Market Details:
Wednesdays from 3:00–6:00 PM Central Park in Downtown Davis Fresh, seasonal produce Artisan goods and prepared foods Local farmers and food makers Family-friendly and open to everyone
Free to attend – shop local and enjoy your Wednesday afternoon at the Davis Farmers

item.title: Davis City Council Meetings — Thu Dec 31, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change.
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance.
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: DJUSD Board Meetings — Thu Jan 7, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
DJUSD Board meetings offer insight on how the school district remains responsive to the community’s values, beliefs, and priorities. The Board meetings occur on every first and third Thursday, in the City of Davis Community Chambers. 23 Russell Boulevard. Public session starts at 6:30 PM. Meetings are cablecast live on Channel 17 (Comcast) or streamed on the DJUSD-TV website.
The Davis Joint Unified School District’s Board of Education is comprised of five community members, responsible for setting district policy, approving the budget, and hiring the superintendent for schools in Davis, California. The agendas for the meetings are posted at least 72 hours in advance.
For more information on special meetings, agendas, public comment, and more, visit the DJUSD Board site.
Source: Hate-Free Together
